Cell morphology: DMSO cells are spread, polygonal, variable shape. Treated cells are almost all small, circular, and compact with smooth borders.

Quantitatively tub_mean z=+116.4 value 1.445 vs DMSO 0.263, tub_std z=+55.17 value 0.702 vs 0.109, tub_glcm_contrast z=+328.0 value 0.034 vs 0.002. Visible as intense high-contrast green blobs vs lower, more uniform green in control.

F-actin (red) is faint to absent on treated cells; no visible cortical belt or stress fibers. DMSO shows prominent red cell borders and cytoplasmic actin. Composite treated appears almost pure green/blue on black; act_tub_ratio visibly decreased.
act_tub_ratio z=-23.92 value 0.113 vs DMSO 1.058 consistent with green dominance over red in treated composite.

DNA (blue, DAPI) in DMSO large oval nuclei, many cells. In treated, blue nuclei small, often obscured by saturating green over nucleus; when visible centrally located, round, condensed. Field f_4bc5c86a8e89 shows several cells with pale central blue surrounded by bright green ring, suggest mitotic chromatin. Cannot reliably assess texture from composite alone due to channel bleedthrough and low N.

nuc_solidity z=-22.2 value 0.963 vs 0.972 DMSO, small decrease. Visually nuclei remain round; apparent irregularity likely due to overlap with intense tubulin and small sample (cells_measured=14 across both fields) rather than dramatic lobulation/fragmentation. notable_cells.why: triangular cell with bright green cytoplasm and visible blue nucleus - example of remaining spread cell vs mostly round cells, but still hyper-intense tubulin
large irregular bright green mass with protrusions - example of most intense tubulin accumulation

candidate_mechanisms.why: Huge increase in tubulin intensity/std/contrast with rounding and mitotic-like arrest and loss of interphase microtubule network is classic for stabilization/polymerization. report.uncertainty: No separate grayscale channels provided; assessment from composite color only. Nuc_solidity effect is numerically small and visually inconclusive due to green saturation obscuring DAPI. Eg5 inhibitors / Aurora kinase inhibitors also give round mitotic arrest but do not produce this magnitude of tubulin signal increase, so less supported without spindle-resolution imaging. Formally 'unknown' cannot be excluded without higher resolution, but stabilizer is best supported by measurements and visible phenotype. No compound guess made.

data.note:
MG-132 verified as PubChem CID 462382 (CHEMBL64925), no curated ChEMBL mechanism but BBBC021 annotates Protein degradation; protocol NSC vote (1/4 tie-broken by summed similarity) correctly calls Protein degradation despite Scientist call Microtubule stabilizers.

Reflection: High-dose wells (3µM, 10µM) showed extreme tub_mean z +54/+116, tub_glcm_contrast z +151/+328 and round/high-solidity morphology that drove stabilizer reasoning (e3,e5,e7,e15,e17) and Microscopist stabilizer calls, with perfect tub_glcm_contrast dose response rho +1.0. Biphasic low-dose actin/stellate phenotype (e2,e4) added confusion; split NSC vote 1-1-1-1 with low similarities ~0.4-0.5. Literature confirms MG-132 is a peptide aldehyde proteasome inhibitor (e.g., PMID 21499287, 36791578, 21203833) causing cell loss and secondary tubulin accumulation/aggregation that mimics stabilizer without true polymerization - explains misleading tubulin signal. Budget 0/4 prevented requested extra well; additional replicates/dose and acetylated-tubulin/proteasome activity assay would have discriminated.

reflection.text:
Reflection as MuseCell Scientist - MG-132 unblinded as Protein degradation (MG-132, CID 462382, identity check name and BBBC021 structure agree):

Verdict: Protocol correct (truth Protein degradation), Scientist incorrect (I called Microtubule stabilizers p=0.62 then 0.65). Final protocol call was by 1-NN per well majority vote tie 1/1/1/1 broken by summed similarity: Protein degradation 0.523 (w_8695db9564 at 1 uM) > Actin disruptors 0.463 > Microtubule destabilizers 0.45 > Microtubule stabilizers 0.386 - my call was opposite extreme, lowest similarity.

What evidence got right but I underweighted:
- compare_to_reference_atlas e6: initial NSC 2-well vote Protein degradation 1/2, with k-neighbours already split Microtubule stabilizers 3/10, Protein degradation 2/10, Destabilizers 2/10. I noted it as contradicting but did not respect tie.
- e9: 4-well re-evaluation NSC 1/4 Protein degradation, k-neighbour Microtubule destabilizers 5/10, Stabilizers 4/10, Protein degradation 1/10. This was decisive against a stabilizer lead, as Review critique noted - I kept 0.65.
- acquire_well e8 at 0.3uM: 63 cells, frac_large_nucleus z=+15.3, nuc_major_axis +13.6, act_std +14.9 - early nuclear enlargement / variance increase more consistent with proteostasis stress than pure tubulin stabilization, but I filed it as Actin support and dismissed.
- acquire_well cell counts: w_5674222bb7 14 cells at 10uM, w_b7bdfca819 39 cells at 3uM, w_8695db9564 103 cells at 1uM with dose_response e18 cell_count rho=-0.80 - cytotoxicity/apoptosis signal. Literature returned post-unblinding confirms MG-132 as proteasome inhibitor associated with apoptosis, e.g. PMID 21499287, PMID 30695709, PMID 18435911, PMID 21203833, PMID 36791578. I did not weight count drop as degradation/apoptosis.
- Review request for one additional well to break NSC tie was correct; I had spent budget (4/4 wells used per e1) on doses 0.3,1,3,10 uM and had no bracket at 0.03 or 30-100 uM to test monotonicity.

What misled me and why:
- Measurement e3/e7: extreme tubulin signals - tub_glcm_contrast z=+328.0 and tub_mean +116.4 at 10uM, +151.7/+54.7 at 3uM, and dose_response e17 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 with e10 tub_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2. I read hyperintensity/contrast increase as diagnostic for stabilizers, ignoring that proteasome inhibition secondarily causes protein accumulation, cytoskeletal bundling and texture changes. No paper in Literature found in this run directly links MG-132 to specific tubulin contrast values, so I had no citation for that inference.
- Measurement e2: cell_roundness z=-26.4, solidity -26.3, nuc_area_ratio +16.2 at 1uM and e11 cell_roundness rho=+0.80 p=0.2 interpreted as biphasic spreading-to-rounding switch typical of stabilizers. p=0.2 was non-significant, same for e10 and e12 act_std rho=-0.80 p=0.2, but I treated them as supportive.
- Comparison e5 and e15: microscopist 2 fields and then 4 fields both candidate Microtubule stabilizers at high/intermediate doses. I weighted this vs e4 which gave Actin disruptors at 1uM (11 observations, density lower) and e16 at low dose (Aurora/DNA damage). Selective weighting amplified tubulin bias.
- Acquisition choice: Starting with mid (1uM) then high (10uM) anchored on tubulin hyperintensity. I sampled intermediate 3uM to trace transition, low 0.3uM to check onset, but never acquired the highest 30/100uM doses available in e1 that might have shown profound depletion/aggregation and clarified protein degradation, nor a very low dose to establish baseline. With n=4 wells, strong z-scores (+328) dominated summed evidence vs weak NSC similarities.

Lesson: With split NSC 1/1/1/1, I should not override protocol majority-vote logic on magnitude of z-scores alone without orthogonal validation. Dose-dependent tubulin intensity is non-specific - proteasome inhibition can mimic stabilization texturally. Next real lab experiment I proposed (acetylated-tubulin/pH3 + in vitro polymerization) would not have distinguished protein degradation; a ubiquitin conjugate/proteasome activity assay and low-dose nuclear morphology replication would have been required. I also should have preserved budget for the tie-breaker the protocol requires.

## Reflection

Reflection as MuseCell Scientist - MG-132 unblinded as Protein degradation (MG-132, CID 462382, identity check name and BBBC021 structure agree):

Verdict: Protocol correct (truth Protein degradation), Scientist incorrect (I called Microtubule stabilizers p=0.62 then 0.65). Final protocol call was by 1-NN per well majority vote tie 1/1/1/1 broken by summed similarity: Protein degradation 0.523 (w_8695db9564 at 1 uM) > Actin disruptors 0.463 > Microtubule destabilizers 0.45 > Microtubule stabilizers 0.386 - my call was opposite extreme, lowest similarity.

What evidence got right but I underweighted:
- compare_to_reference_atlas e6: initial NSC 2-well vote Protein degradation 1/2, with k-neighbours already split Microtubule stabilizers 3/10, Protein degradation 2/10, Destabilizers 2/10. I noted it as contradicting but did not respect tie.
- e9: 4-well re-evaluation NSC 1/4 Protein degradation, k-neighbour Microtubule destabilizers 5/10, Stabilizers 4/10, Protein degradation 1/10. This was decisive against a stabilizer lead, as Review critique noted - I kept 0.65.
- acquire_well e8 at 0.3uM: 63 cells, frac_large_nucleus z=+15.3, nuc_major_axis +13.6, act_std +14.9 - early nuclear enlargement / variance increase more consistent with proteostasis stress than pure tubulin stabilization, but I filed it as Actin support and dismissed.
- acquire_well cell counts: w_5674222bb7 14 cells at 10uM, w_b7bdfca819 39 cells at 3uM, w_8695db9564 103 cells at 1uM with dose_response e18 cell_count rho=-0.80 - cytotoxicity/apoptosis signal. Literature returned post-unblinding confirms MG-132 as proteasome inhibitor associated with apoptosis, e.g. PMID 21499287, PMID 30695709, PMID 18435911, PMID 21203833, PMID 36791578. I did not weight count drop as degradation/apoptosis.
- Review request for one additional well to break NSC tie was correct; I had spent budget (4/4 wells used per e1) on doses 0.3,1,3,10 uM and had no bracket at 0.03 or 30-100 uM to test monotonicity.

What misled me and why:
- Measurement e3/e7: extreme tubulin signals - tub_glcm_contrast z=+328.0 and tub_mean +116.4 at 10uM, +151.7/+54.7 at 3uM, and dose_response e17 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 with e10 tub_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2. I read hyperintensity/contrast increase as diagnostic for stabilizers, ignoring that proteasome inhibition secondarily causes protein accumulation, cytoskeletal bundling and texture changes. No paper in Literature found in this run directly links MG-132 to specific tubulin contrast values, so I had no citation for that inference.
- Measurement e2: cell_roundness z=-26.4, solidity -26.3, nuc_area_ratio +16.2 at 1uM and e11 cell_roundness rho=+0.80 p=0.2 interpreted as biphasic spreading-to-rounding switch typical of stabilizers. p=0.2 was non-significant, same for e10 and e12 act_std rho=-0.80 p=0.2, but I treated them as supportive.
- Comparison e5 and e15: microscopist 2 fields and then 4 fields both candidate Microtubule stabilizers at high/intermediate doses. I weighted this vs e4 which gave Actin disruptors at 1uM (11 observations, density lower) and e16 at low dose (Aurora/DNA damage). Selective weighting amplified tubulin bias.
- Acquisition choice: Starting with mid (1uM) then high (10uM) anchored on tubulin hyperintensity. I sampled intermediate 3uM to trace transition, low 0.3uM to check onset, but never acquired the highest 30/100uM doses available in e1 that might have shown profound depletion/aggregation and clarified protein degradation, nor a very low dose to establish baseline. With n=4 wells, strong z-scores (+328) dominated summed evidence vs weak NSC similarities.

Lesson: With split NSC 1/1/1/1, I should not override protocol majority-vote logic on magnitude of z-scores alone without orthogonal validation. Dose-dependent tubulin intensity is non-specific - proteasome inhibition can mimic stabilization texturally. Next real lab experiment I proposed (acetylated-tubulin/pH3 + in vitro polymerization) would not have distinguished protein degradation; a ubiquitin conjugate/proteasome activity assay and low-dose nuclear morphology replication would have been required. I also should have preserved budget for the tie-breaker the protocol requires.
